UI-only modeling completed.
Exact export and interaction parity failed.

Built a dimensioned 2D sketch and four 3D solids in each application using ten distinct modeling tools. No FeatureScript was used. Onshape exports are cached, and the Chili3D project is included.

Compared every original byte without normalization. First differences occur at byte offsets 22 (STEP) and 3 (DXF), counting from zero. STEP exporter headers and encoding differ; DXF also differs in line endings, entity ordering and numeric formatting. Full SHA-256 hashes are in raw-comparison.json.

Secondary geometry check: consistent after axis correction.
All four part pairs produced zero-volume Boolean differences in both directions in OCCT 8.0. Maximum bounding-coordinate difference was approximately 0.0000001 mm. Both DXFs contain the same 20 × 20 mm rectangle within floating-point precision. These checks do not satisfy raw byte equality.

Click an image to inspect the complete UI. Cameras and display settings differ.

Observed interaction and result differences
  • Shell: Onshape accepted 1 mm inward; Chili3D reported “shell failed.” Both continued successfully at 0.5 mm. Chili3D also replaced the parametric feature chain with an editable solid.
  • Mirror and patterns: Onshape selects planes or axes; Chili3D uses point-based commands. The first circular copy had a different placement because of the selected/inferred axis. Recreating it with a fixed XY workplane and the same offset axis corrected the geometry.
  • Union: Chili3D’s Fuse could not select the editable shell outputs. Preselecting a part and invoking Join succeeded.
  • Numeric move: Chili3D threw a view error when coordinates were entered before hovering in the viewport. Restarting and hovering first succeeded.
  • Dimensioning: Onshape scaled the entire sketch after the first dimension; Chili3D changed only the dimensioned width. Both ended at 20 × 20 mm.

Failure evidence and recovery notes

1 mm shell failure; continued at 0.5 mm in both applications.

Numeric input error before viewport hover; recovered through the UI.

The first circular-pattern files are preserved in initial-run/. The final files use the corrected axis. A native project download initially stalled during concurrent development rebuilds; reopening the saved document and retrying succeeded. Its cause was not isolated. Unrelated compile overlays interrupted the session and were not counted as CAD parity defects.

Provenance and reproducibility

Model construction and exports used visible UI controls, pointer actions and keyboard entry. Browser DOM inspection and control focus assisted automation. Offline code only verified the downloaded files; it did not construct or substitute either exported model. Onshape STEP and DXF were each downloaded once after model completion. The raw files remain unchanged.

run.json records inputs, settings and download times. geometry-inspection.json records the secondary checks. Run node artifacts/cad-ui-parity-testing/verify-exports.mjs in the repository to repeat verification. This specimen is not comprehensive UI conformance coverage.
